body: Scout race evidence for candidate/authorization lifecycle: I posted superseding align candidate 48d9bce after catching a doc contradiction; the chief had already landed the prior functional candidate f4c1a05 roughly 20 seconds earlier, and our follow-up request/authorization messages crossed again. Both actors acted correctly from their visible state; the result required a second doc-only candidate b3d3571 and another compile gate. This is a concrete case for first-class candidate state plus atomic conditional land authorization: a supersede transition should invalidate a not-yet-landed predecessor, while an already-landed predecessor should make supersede return a structured already-landed result and create/offer a fix-forward.
